subject: History

source.title: National curriculum in England: history programmes of study

note: Controlled paraphrases of the statutory programme of study. Example content marked non-statutory by the source is not represented as a statutory requirement.

KS3: Ideas, political power, industry and empire 1745-1901

KS1.summary: Develop awareness of the past using chronological language, placing studied people and events within a simple sequence and identifying similarities and differences between periods.
Explore changes within living memory and significant events beyond living memory, using them to identify features of change in national or wider life.
Learn about significant people whose achievements contributed to national or international history and compare aspects of life across periods.
Study significant historical events, people and places connected with the pupils' own locality.
Ask and answer historical questions using stories and other sources, recognising ways evidence about the past is discovered and represented.

KS2.summary: Build chronologically secure knowledge of British, local and world history, identifying connections, contrasts, trends, change, cause, similarity, difference and significance.
Study changes in Britain from the Stone Age to the Iron Age.
Study the Roman Empire and its impact on Britain.
Study the settlement of Britain by Anglo-Saxons and Scots.
Study the Viking and Anglo-Saxon struggle for the Kingdom of England to the time of Edward the Confessor.
Carry out a local history study that develops understanding of change and significance through evidence from the locality.
Study an aspect or theme in British history that extends chronological knowledge beyond 1066.
Study the emergence of the earliest civilisations and complete a depth study of one specified ancient civilisation.
Study Greek life and achievements and consider their influence on the western world.
Study a specified non-European society that provides a contrast with British history.
Develop historically valid questions, construct informed responses, select relevant information and understand that knowledge of the past is built from a range of sources.

KS3.summary: Extend chronologically secure knowledge of British, local and world history, making connections, drawing contrasts and analysing trends over periods and longer timescales.
Study the development of Church, state and society in Medieval Britain from 1066 to 1509.
Study the development of Church, state and society in Britain from 1509 to 1745.

KS3.domain: Ideas, political power, industry and empire 1745-1901
KS3.summary: Study ideas, political power, industry and empire in Britain from 1745 to 1901.
Study challenges for Britain, Europe and the wider world from 1901 to the present, including the Holocaust.
Complete a local history study that deepens understanding through evidence, chronology and connections with wider history.
Study an aspect or theme in British history that consolidates and extends chronological knowledge, including possible themes such as political power, landscape, migration or turning points.
Study at least one significant society or issue in world history and its interconnections with other world developments.
Pursue historically valid enquiries, use sources rigorously to make historical claims, construct evidentially supported accounts and examine contrasting interpretations of the past.
